on_device.stays_on_the_device: These stay on your device until you uninstall the game or remove them. If you enter a license key, your license key and a secret this device chose also go to the game's server. If you use friend groups, your private code and your scores from games that count also go to the game's server.

network.every_request: Sent over HTTPS to this server, except the connectivity checks, which go to the address each names, as plain HTTP that carries nothing about the player.
network.outside_services: The game has no analytics, crash-reporting, advertising or attribution services.

requests.when: When a player enters a license key, and at each start until setdef's server has answered, so the key moves to this device. Never on a copy sold by a store.

requests.when: Once each time the game starts, on a device holding a license key, to learn whether the key has moved to another device.
Only when setdef's server gave no valid proof at a start: to tell setdef being gone from the internet being down. Apple's connectivity check, which answers the same page to everyone.
As the one before, only if Apple's check did not answer as expected. Google's connectivity check, which answers an empty page to everyone.
As the one before, only if neither Apple's nor Google's check answered as expected. Microsoft's connectivity check, which answers the same line to everyone.

purchases: When you buy Pro in a store's copy, your purchase goes straight from your device to Apple or Google. The game sends nothing about it. In a copy from setdef's website, you buy in your browser, and the license key you are sent is checked by the game itself. While setdef's server answers, the key and a random secret go to it, so the key works on one device at a time.

apple.ip_addresses: The server's proxy and request log see the IP address of every request, and its rate-limit notes can hold it. The game neither reads nor sends it as data, and it is not used to work out a location. How long each is kept is stated by the server's own privacy policy. Apple's list has no IP-address category, so it is not among the data types; if the maintainer or Apple's review reads "Device ID" as covering it, add that, linked and for App Functionality.

google.ip_addresses: The server's proxy and request log see the IP address of every request, and its rate-limit notes can hold it. The game neither reads nor sends it as data, and it is not used to work out a location. How long each is kept is stated by the server's own privacy policy. The maintainer decides whether to list it under Device or other IDs.
